Class ReferenceImport

java.lang.Object
global.thalion.ttio.genomics.ReferenceImport
public final class ReferenceImport extends Object
Reference-FASTA value class staged for embedding into a .tio container.

A ReferenceImport is the parsed result of a reference-FASTA file (many short or long chromosome records, no quality scores). It carries the chromosome names, per-chromosome sequence bytes, and a content-MD5 suitable for the @md5 attribute on /study/references/<uri>/ groups.

Cross-language equivalents: Python ttio.genomic.reference_import.ReferenceImport, Objective-C TTIOReferenceImport.

The MD5 algorithm sorts chromosomes by name (so the digest is order-invariant), then concatenates the per-chromosome sequence_bytes verbatim (case-preserving, no framing) and digests the result. Cross-language byte-equal. Unified in v1.1.0 with the REF_DIFF_V2 auto-embed writer's stamp; the previous name-framed form is gone.

    • computeMd5

      public static byte[] computeMd5(List<String> chromosomes, List<byte[]> sequences)
      Compute the canonical content-MD5 over a chromosome set. The algorithm sorts by name (order-invariant), then concatenates the per-chromosome sequence bytes verbatim (case-preserving, no framing) into an MD5 digest. Matches the REF_DIFF_V2 auto-embed writer's stamp byte-for-byte (unified in v1.1.0).

    • readFromGroup

      public static ReferenceImport readFromGroup(StorageGroup refGroup)
      Read an embedded reference from /study/references/<uri>/.

      Layout (matches the writer in SpectralDataset.embedReferencesForRuns):

      • refGroup attribute reference_uri = the reference URI; falls back to refGroup.name().
      • refGroup attribute md5 = lowercase-hex content MD5; preserved verbatim into the returned ReferenceImport so byte-for-byte round-trip is maintained.
      • refGroup/chromosomes/ = sub-group containing one child per chromosome.
      • refGroup/chromosomes/<name>/data = UINT8 dataset of sequence bytes (case-preserving).

      Chromosomes are returned in the order StorageGroup.childNames() reports them — the writer sorts alphabetically before persisting, so for any file written by this library the order is alphabetic.

      Parameters:
      refGroup - the /study/references/<uri>/ group
      Returns:
      a fully-populated ReferenceImport
      Since:
      1.1.0

    • writeToDataset

      public void writeToDataset(SpectralDataset dataset, boolean overwrite)
      Embed this reference at /study/references/<uri>/ inside dataset's open storage backing.

      Layout (cross-language byte-equal — matches Python's ReferenceImport.write_to_dataset and the canonical embed-helper writer used by embedReference=true runs):

      • /study/references/<uri>/ group with @md5 (32-char lowercase hex) and @reference_uri attributes.
      • chromosomes/<name>/ sub-group per chromosome, in alphabetic order, with an @length (int64) attribute.
      • chromosomes/<name>/data UINT8 ZLIB-compressed dataset of sequence bytes.

      If a reference with the same uri is already embedded and overwrite is false, throws IllegalStateException (mirrors Python's FileExistsError). When overwrite is true, the existing group is deleted first.

      Parameters:
      dataset - open dataset; must expose a writable StorageProvider via SpectralDataset.provider().
      overwrite - if true, replace any existing reference under the same URI.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if overwrite=false and a reference with the same URI is already embedded, or if the dataset has no open writable provider.
      Since:
      1.1.0

    • writeToDataset

      public void writeToDataset(SpectralDataset dataset, boolean overwrite, ProgressSink progress)
      Overload of writeToDataset(SpectralDataset, boolean) that fires progress.onProgress(i+1, totalChromosomes) after each chromosome's HDF5 group + attributes + dataset are written. Slow paths (whale + plant genomes with thousands of contigs) report visible mid-stream progress; the fast paths (single-chromosome refs) fire once.
      Since:
      1.3.0
